summary: Edge NAT handshake interruption results in incomplete numbered checklist + missing embedded image on SSE stream
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that long SSE streaming responses intermittently terminate with the last numbered checklist item missing and a final embedded image URL omitted. This happens after their users experience a network path change (ISP NAT port refresh / IP rebind).

Impact: Several LuminaDocs customers see corrupted docs: a numbered checklist in the final paragraphs is cut at item 3 of 4 and the final image embed (markdown ![diagram](...)) never arrives. Problem first reported 2026-03-10; frequency ~2-3% of long (>= 2k token) streams for their users.

Environment: production (us-east), customer on dedicated plan with VPC egress through their ISP (residential & corporate). Affected model: gpt-open-xt-4b.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Start SSE request that streams a long markdown document containing a 4-item numbered checklist and an inline image URL near the end.
2) While stream active, client environment briefly changes IP (customer observed ISP NAT port refresh during mobile tethering).
3) Client reconnects automatically. SSE resumes, but stream ends with checklist missing last bullet and no image URL.

Observed behavior: On reconnect the SSE stream completes without an explicit end marker in the original session; the client sees the final chunk cut off between bullets (partial sentence) and image markdown absent. Server logs show the upstream worker closed the old socket and a new socket established with a different connection-id; resume handshake attempted but resume_offset reported by client does not match server session snapshot (resume rejected).

Expected behavior: Stream resume should deliver the remaining tokens (or clearly return an error) so the client can render the complete checklist and image; resume should be tolerant to customer NAT port refresh where only 5-tuple changes but session identity remains logically the same via resume token.

Logs / snippets: (sanitized):
- edge-proxy: connection closed, reason=half-close, remote_ip=198.51.100.23:52345, conn_id=wrk-1172
- serving-runtime: resume-token=abc123 ttl_expiry=2026-03-10T12:03:05Z, compare_offset=15670, client_offset=15670, session_state=sealed
- worker: flush_tail: aborted before final event, kv_cache_seal=true, client_resume_reject: mismatch-epoch

Customer-supplied curl sequence (simplified):
- initial SSE: GET /v1/streams?resume_token=abc123 -> stream begins
- simulate NAT rebind (tether off/on)
- new SSE connect with same resume_token -> server responded 200 but returned truncated body
investigation_notes: 03/10 14:12 - Replicated with local harness: performed a simulated NAT port change (docker NAT) while streaming a 2k+ token markdown response; observed identical truncation when server's resume grace window expired mid-flush.
03/10 15:02 - Edge logs show half-close by LB during keepalive jitter window; worker marked session sealed prior to tail flush (kv_cache_seal flag).

03/11 09:20 - Resume handshake path uses resume-token TTL vs ephemeral cookie; in customer's case resume-token was valid but session epoch mismatch caused resume rejection path to perform a best-effort finalization that did not deliver remaining buffered tokens to new connection.

03/11 11:00 - Hypothesis: NAT rebind caused client to present same resume_token but a different TCP 5-tuple; edge proxy policy considered it 'new session' and triggered worker-side seal, and the code path that moves buffered tail to new socket requires matching epoch which may be cleared by short TTLs and aggressive sealing during half-close.
comments: 2026-03-10 - from lumina-support@luminadocs.com: 'We see users losing the last checklist item and final image on posts when their phone swaps from wifi->cellular. Attached a packet capture and a screenshot.'
2026-03-10 - Support (Ava): 'Thanks — we've reproduced in-house with a NAT rebind test. We're escalating to runtime/edge teams to confirm resume semantics.'

2026-03-11 - Eng (Ravi): 'Preliminary root cause: worker seals session on half-close during keepalive jitter. The resume path rejects epoch mismatch and the fallback finalization doesn't stream the buffered tail to the resume connection. I opened PR to add graceful tail-forwarding and extend resume grace window.'
2026-03-12 - Customer (LuminaDocs): 'Can you suggest a temporary workaround while you patch? Our product UX relies on complete checklists.'

2026-03-12 - Support (Ava): 'Workaround: ask clients to include a client-side explicit resume_offset in reconnect requests (we can accept earlier offsets) and increase client reconnection backoff to allow server tail-flush (~3s). We'll notify when patch is deployed.'
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 - Mitigation deployed to canary: increased resume grace window from 2s -> 6s and added code path to forward buffered tail to new connection when resume_token matches but epoch differs. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8543.

Temporary customer workaround: instruct users to set client reconnect backoff to 3s and include resume_offset (if available) when rejoining the stream; client SDK patch pending to automate this behavior.

Next steps: roll the canary change to prod us-east after 48h monitoring; add unit tests for NAT path migration and an integration test that toggles client IP mid-stream. Postmortem and permanent fix to be tracked in INT-3309 for changes to sealing semantics.
notes_for_ops: If rolling forward to prod, coordinate with edge LB team to ensure no aggressive keepalive pruning during rollout window. Monitor SSE tail-drop metric (stream.tail_drop_count) and customer-reported incidents for LuminaDocs for 72 hours post-deploy.
